Hi Ben / Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the MSA + security exhibit and had a few open items they want to align on before we proceed to procurement: 

- SOC 2 assertions: confirmation of which control set (Type II, and which date range) will be provided.
- Pen test language: request that the MSA include a 30-day notice window for scheduled tests and a limited scope clause for tenant impact.
- Audit access: specific evidence artifacts we can expect (control descriptions, tickets, sample logs) and a proposal for a weekly evidence cadence during onboarding.
- Evidence retention & redaction: which artifacts are redacted for PII and the retention period.

Can you propose a short runbook or sprint-style cadence (1–2 week sprints) for evidence collection and one owner per lane (SOC2, pen-test, logs)? Attaching our redline notes — we flagged a couple of wording items in the security exhibit.

Happy to set a 30–45 minute sync this week to walk the redlines with legal if that helps.

Appreciate it,
Samantha

Thanks team — I reviewed Samantha's redlines and Ben's proposal. A few legal notes and suggested edits for the MSA security exhibit language: 

- Pen test clause: we will accept a 30-day notice for customer-initiated tests, with the caveat that production-impacting tests must be scheduled during pre-agreed maintenance windows. Suggested language: "Customer shall provide Provider with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice for planned penetration testing of the Service. Provider will coordinate to schedule such testing during mutually agreed windows to avoid material impact to production operations."

- Limited scope: add an explicit carve-out that excludes simulated denial-of-service and social engineering against Provider employees without prior coordination.

- Evidence access: recommend enumerating artifact buckets instead of open-ended "reasonable access." Example buckets: (a) SOC 2 report and bridge letter; (b) sample system configuration and change logs for named services; (c) anonymized request/response logs (30-day window) and artifact index. Requests for raw forensic access should be escalated to legal and provided under an NDA and inspection appointment.

- Redaction & retention: propose linking to the runbook (not in the MSA): retention periods by artifact type; redaction standards (hashing/zeroing PII) and a takedown process. Keeps contract concise while operationalizing specifics in a runbook.

- Audit notice timeline: suggest adding a 90-day onramp for any audit operations after signature (gives teams time to prepare).

If Laura can confirm the SOC2 report date and whether a bridge letter is available, I can produce a redlined MSA snippet to share with Samantha before the call. I also attached the draft language I plan to propose.

Karthik
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: msa_security_language_snippet.docx
